target_customer: Construction teams, later security screening and cargo inspection
problem: Mapping pipes, wiring and structure inside walls and ceilings is slow and invasive; the company images them with radio waves from across a room.
business_model: Hardware imaging systems with software (pricing not public)

founders.name: Bilgehan Avser
founders.background_notes: YC page: led antenna technologies at Apple, head of technology at Humane through HP acquisition, 35+ patents.

founders.name: Brian Huppi
education: UMass Amherst, civil and electrical engineering
founders.background_notes: YC page: early iPhone prototypes, co-inventor of first generation Nest Learning Thermostat.

founders.name: George McLean
education: MIT and UC Berkeley, physics degrees
founders.background_notes: YC page: applied physicist, semiconductor imaging and medical devices.

competitors.name: Walabot (Vayyar)
competitors.what: Consumer RF wall scanner, about 10 cm depth

competitors.name: Bosch D-TECT 200 C
competitors.what: Radar wall and floor scanner for cables, rebar, pipes

technical_complexity.rationale: Through-wall imaging with 1 mm point clouds across wall types needs RF, hardware and signal processing breakthroughs; launch materials do not show performance across conditions.

defensibility.rationale: Deep RF hardware expertise and patents of the team, but handheld radar scanners exist.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents sell short-range scanners; none observed offering room-scale imaging. No outcome yet.

market_need_then: Construction relies on drawings and manual scans to locate hidden utilities; the wedge targets this, plus defense and cargo uses mentioned by the company.

branding.domain_note: Redirects ae-dyn.com to appliedelectrodynamics.com (301); not verified further as the destination page fetch was rate limited.

brand_strength.rationale: Product name WaveSight is clear and launched with demo coverage (July 30 2026 article), while the corporate name is long and generic. Team pedigree drives press more than brand.

outcome_analysis: Applied Electrodynamics is a Summer 2026 hardware company with no outcome yet. The founders include veterans of Apple and Humane with iPhone and Nest credentials, which gives credibility on hard hardware. It unveiled WaveSight in July 2026. Risks are hardware performance proof, long sales cycles in construction and capital intensity.
notes: Dealroom lists a $125K seed, unverified aggregator, not a round. The company website redirect target could not be fetched because the domain safety check was rate limited. Competitor entries are current products, dated loosely, and no direct room-scale competitor was found.
